verdict.rationale: AMD provides an extensive first-party toolchain for this chip's AI/NPU capabilities — Ryzen AI Software docs, ONNX Runtime + Vitis AI EP, Quark quantization toolkit, Lemonade SDK, GAIA agent framework, AI Analyzer, xrt-smi — plus explicit OS support for Windows, RHEL and Ubuntu, and community reports of real-world Linux/llama.cpp usage. However this tooling is largely AMD's own proprietary stack rather than evidence of broad mainstream compiler/toolchain maturity (e.g., standard GCC/LLVM optimization guidance), and community commentary focuses on performance/benchmarking gaps and missing Pro features (ECC reporting) rather than affirming tier-one developer-ecosystem status. Missing for 10: independent corroboration of general (non-AI) compiler/toolchain maturity, evidence of broader ecosystem adoption beyond AMD's own SDKs, and explicit official architecture-level optimization guidance outside the AI stack.
